origin.description: Named characters for ticks, arrows, and line drawing. UTF-8 when Unicode output is on, ASCII otherwise.
origin.details: symbol is an active binding. It reads cli.unicode, and otherwise is_utf8_output().
origin.value: The selected symbol list. In Python, index it by name.
origin.example:
options(cli.unicode = TRUE)
cat(symbol$tick, " SUCCESS\n", symbol$cross, " FAILURE\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Named characters for ticks, arrows, and line drawing. UTF-8 when Unicode output is on, ASCII otherwise.
translation.details: symbol is an active binding. It reads cli.unicode, and otherwise is_utf8_output().
translation.value: The selected symbol list. In Python, index it by name.
translation.example:
from cli import options, symbol
options(**{"cli.unicode": True})
print(symbol["tick"] + " SUCCESS")
print(symbol["cross"] + " FAILURE")
